goal.title: Goal
goal.briefing.brighteningSun: The Sun keeps brightening: weathering is starving the air of CO₂, land life is thinning, and a runaway greenhouse will boil the oceans near 7 billion years. Preserve liquid oceans and complex life until the planet is 8.1 billion years old. Sunshades can dim sunlight by at most 8%; cloud and surface controls have modest ranges.
goal.briefing.snowball: This world is locked beneath global ice. Use CO₂, volcanism and albedo to bring ice below 15% and temperature above 5 °C, then hold both for 5 million years. You have 1 billion years.
goal.briefing.cradle: Nurture this microbial world through complex evolution until a species becomes sentient. Complex-life extinction or a two-billion-year delay ends the attempt.
goal.keepPlayingHint: Continue this planet as a sandbox after the outcome
goal.newPlanetHint: Open the menu to start another planet
goal.reason.oceansLost: The oceans were lost to space.
goal.reason.survivedBrightening: Liquid oceans and complex life survived the brightening Sun.
goal.reason.snowballThawed: The global ice retreated and the warm climate remained stable.
goal.briefing.terraformMars: Mars is cold, dry and nearly airless. Build CO₂ and nitrogen generators to thicken the air, drop ice meteors for water, add oxygen and a biome factory for plants. Reach 0.5 bar, 5 °C, open sea and growing plants, and hold them for 10 million years. You have 500 million years; impacts and eruptions destroy devices.
goal.reason.terraformed: The planet became warm, wet and green, and stayed that way.
scenarioHelp.terraformMars: Goal: make present-day Mars habitable with generators, ice meteors and a biome factory.
toolHelp.iceMeteor: Drops a ~200 km icy comet: a crater and about 10 m of global water on an Earth-sized planet, more on a small one.
toolHelp.co2Generator: Builds a factory that keeps releasing CO₂ (about 0.01 bar per million years on Earth).
toolHelp.n2Generator: Builds a factory that keeps releasing nitrogen (about 0.01 bar per million years on Earth).
toolHelp.o2Generator: Builds a factory that keeps releasing oxygen; without life it slowly reacts away again.
toolHelp.co2Scrubber: Builds a plant that turns atmospheric CO₂ into rock (about 0.5 bar per million years), stopping at 280 ppm.
toolHelp.biomeFactory: Builds a factory that keeps sowing land plants nearby wherever they can grow.
stat.lifeHint: What a distant telescope would see: oxygen and methane together reveal life; one alone is only a hint
scenarioHelp.stoneAge: Goal: lead a young stone-age people from one island through every age to Exodus.
scenarioHelp.cambrian: An Earth-like planet as the Cambrian begins: animals in the seas, bare land. No goal.
goal.briefing.exodus: A people of mammals has just become sentient on one island. Help them spread, survive plagues and wars, and advance through all seven ages until they leave the planet. A collapse of the civilization or 300,000 years without Exodus ends the attempt.
goal.reason.exodus: The civilization left the planet in an Exodus.

help.title: Help
help.howToPlayText: Run time to let the planet evolve, switch map layers to inspect its systems, and use tools or model windows to shape its future. Goal scenarios show their objectives in the Goal tab.
help.aboutText: Geogenesis {version} is a planet simulation inspired by SimEarth.
help.section.overviewHint: How to play and keyboard shortcuts
help.section.glossaryHint: Search terms used by the simulation
guide.notAvailable: This view is not available in the current scenario
guide.geosphere.title: Geosphere and plates
guide.geosphere.summary: Moving plates recycle crust, open oceans and raise mountains. Rain, rivers and ice then wear relief down.
guide.geosphere.loop: mantle heat → plate motion → uplift → erosion → lower relief
guide.geosphere.controls: Plate speed, volcanism and erosion controls change the rates. Terrain, volcano, meteor and earthquake tools reshape local crust.
guide.geosphere.views: Terrain shows relief and water; Plates shows moving crust; Volcanism shows ridges, arcs and hotspots. Land and sea-level charts show long changes.
guide.climate.title: Climate and seasons
guide.climate.summary: Sunlight, reflection, greenhouse gases and heat transport set temperature. Tilt makes seasons, while oceans soften them.
guide.climate.loop: warming → less ice → lower albedo → more absorbed sunlight → warming
guide.climate.controls: Star brightness, axial tilt, greenhouse strength, cloud reflection and surface reflection act here. CO₂ tools also change climate.
guide.climate.views: Temperature, Seasons and Clouds map the response. Temperature, ice and runaway-margin charts reveal trends.
guide.atmosphereWater.title: Atmosphere and water
guide.atmosphereWater.summary: Air pressure moves heat and water around the planet. Water cycles through ocean, vapour, rain, snow and ice, and can escape to space.
guide.atmosphereWater.loop: warming → more water vapour → stronger greenhouse → warming
guide.atmosphereWater.controls: Rainfall and air–sea heat controls change the cycle. Gas generators, scrubbers and ice meteors alter atmospheric or water inventories.
guide.atmosphereWater.views: Pressure, Precipitation and Clouds show circulation and water. Pressure, water and oxygen charts track the whole atmosphere.
guide.carbon.title: Carbon cycle
guide.carbon.summary: Volcanoes add CO₂. Rock weathering, ocean-floor reactions and organic burial remove it, creating a slow climate thermostat.
guide.carbon.loop: warming → faster weathering → less CO₂ → cooling
guide.carbon.controls: Volcanism, erosion and rainfall affect natural fluxes. CO₂ tools, generators and scrubbers add or remove carbon directly.
guide.carbon.views: Volcanism and Biomes show major sources and land sinks. CO₂ and carbon-flux charts show whether the air is gaining carbon.
guide.oceans.title: Oceans
guide.oceans.summary: Winds drive currents and upwelling. Oceans carry heat, feed marine life and exchange oxygen and carbon with the air.
guide.oceans.loop: wind → currents and upwelling → heat and nutrients → climate and marine life
guide.oceans.controls: Climate and rainfall controls affect ocean temperature and supply. Ice meteors add water; atmospheric tools indirectly change ocean chemistry.
guide.oceans.views: Ocean Currents, Ocean Oxygen and Nutrients show movement and habitat. Oxygen, acidity and sea-level charts show global change.
guide.life.title: Life and evolution
guide.life.summary: Life spreads only through suitable habitat. New classes evolve from established ones; plants then alter albedo, weathering and oxygen.
guide.life.loop: plants → oxygen and weathering → new habitats → more complex life
guide.life.controls: Evolution pace, reproduction and thermal tolerance shape the biosphere. Place Life and Monolith tools can intervene locally.
guide.life.views: Biomes shows habitat, Life shows the most advanced class and Diversity shows communities. Life and biodiversity charts show progress.
guide.turningPoints.title: Turning points
guide.turningPoints.summary: Oxygenation, rapid warming, impacts, anoxic seas and extinctions can redirect evolution. Survivors may radiate into emptied niches.
guide.turningPoints.loop: disturbance → extinction → open niches → recovery and radiation
guide.turningPoints.controls: Climate, carbon and disaster controls change the stresses. Meteor, volcano and fire tools can trigger abrupt disruption.
guide.turningPoints.views: Ocean Oxygen, Clathrates and Hazard reveal risks. Biodiversity, dust and acidity charts expose sudden changes.
guide.civilization.title: Civilization and energy
guide.civilization.summary: A sentient species settles, produces energy and advances through technology. Its choices affect population, pollution, war risk and climate.
guide.civilization.loop: energy → growth and technology → resource use and pollution → stability
guide.civilization.controls: Choose an energy mix and investments in the Civilization window. Monolith can advance a society; disasters can damage it.
guide.civilization.views: Civilization and Hazard show settlement and exposure. Population, pollution and fuel charts show whether growth is sustainable.
guide.disasters.title: Disasters
guide.disasters.summary: Tectonics, weather, impacts and eruptions create hazards. They damage settlements and can briefly disturb climate and life.
guide.disasters.loop: hazard → damage and dust → lost capacity → recovery
guide.disasters.controls: Natural disaster switches enable each family. Earthquake, hurricane, tidal-wave, fire, meteor and volcano tools create directed events.
guide.disasters.views: Hazard maps long-term exposure; Volcanism shows eruption regions. Dust and biodiversity charts show wider consequences.
guide.goals.title: Goals
guide.goals.summary: Goal scenarios have a live checklist, deadline and score. Meet every required condition, including any hold time, before the deadline.
guide.goals.loop: inspect checklist → change one system → run time → check the response
guide.goals.controls: Use the current-task card, model controls and tools. Some scenarios restrict control ranges or provide special devices.
guide.goals.views: The Goal tab has exact values and time remaining. Choose layers and charts that match the unmet checklist conditions.
glossary.abiogenesis.definition: The natural origin of the first life from non-living chemistry.
glossary.aerosol.definition: Tiny airborne particles that can reflect sunlight and cool the surface.
glossary.albedo.definition: The share of incoming light a surface reflects; ice and clouds have high albedo.
glossary.anoxia.definition: A lack of usable oxygen, especially in ocean water.
glossary.biome.definition: A broad habitat type set mainly by temperature, water and vegetation.
glossary.biosignature.definition: A remotely visible chemical clue to life, such as oxygen together with methane.
glossary.clathrate.definition: Ice-like crystals that store methane in cold ground or shallow seafloor sediment.
glossary.Exodus.definition: The final technology milestone, when civilization leaves its planet.
glossary.GEL.definition: Global equivalent layer: a water volume expressed as an even depth over the whole planet.
glossary.Great Oxidation.definition: The first major rise of atmospheric oxygen after biological production overcame surface sinks.
glossary.Hadley cell.definition: Tropical overturning circulation: air rises near the equator and sinks in the subtropics.
glossary.hazard.definition: The long-term chance and severity of a damaging natural event.
glossary.hold time.definition: How long every required goal condition must remain satisfied at once.
glossary.ITCZ.definition: The Intertropical Convergence Zone, a shifting rainy belt where tropical winds meet.
glossary.large igneous province.definiti: A rare, vast outpouring of lava that can release carbon and aerosols for a long time.
glossary.mass extinction.definition: A rapid global loss of much of complex life compared with its recent peak.
glossary.objective.definition: One measurable condition in a scenario's goal checklist.
glossary.outgassing.definition: Release of gases, especially CO₂, from a planet's interior through volcanism.
glossary.partial pressure.definition: The pressure contributed by one gas within a mixture of gases.
glossary.plate tectonics.definition: Motion and recycling of rigid crustal plates over the mantle.
glossary.pollution.definition: Persistent industrial contamination that stresses life and civilization.
glossary.runaway greenhouse.definition: A state where a wet atmosphere cannot radiate enough heat, so oceans evaporate and warming accelerates.
glossary.score.definition: A goal scenario's measure of performance, based on progress and time.
glossary.sentience.definition: The evolutionary step at which an animal species can found a civilization.
glossary.upwelling.definition: Ocean water rising from depth, usually cold and rich in nutrients.
glossary.water vapour.definition: Water in gas form; it is also a strong greenhouse gas.
glossary.weathering.definition: Chemical breakdown of rock that consumes atmospheric CO₂ when liquid water is present.
glossary.Ω energy.definition: The gameplay resource spent when using map tools; it replenishes over time.
tour.backHint: Go to the previous tour step
tour.nextHint: Go to the next tour step
tour.restartHint: Close Help and show the guided tour again
tour.step.map: The map is your main view. Choose a layer above it, hover to inspect a place, and use overlays to combine information.
tour.step.time: Play evolves the planet. Pause to inspect it, Step once, and choose a display speed. Simulated years per step change with the era.
tour.step.vitals: These global readings summarize climate, air, life, ice, the star and your Ω tool energy. Hover any reading for its meaning.
tour.step.windows: These windows explain and control the geosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, civilization and planet. Their ? buttons open the matching guide page.
tour.step.tool: Pick a tool here, then click the map. Its Ω cost is shown on the button; click the selected tool again or press Escape to put it down.
tour.step.era: Early geological steps cover millions of years. As complex life and civilization appear, eras change and each step becomes shorter.
tour.step.goal: This card says what matters now. In goal scenarios, open the Goal tab for exact targets, progress, deadline and score. Meet all conditions to finish.
sound.title: Sound
sound.description: Procedural music follows the planet's era. Defaults: master 70%, music 25%, effects 65%.
